shiva-tripura.ref: pathigam 1.131 (திருமுதுகுன்றம்), verse 4; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: The gods become Shiva's chariot, Mount Meru the bow, the serpent Vasuki the string and Vishnu the fire-tipped arrow; he reduces the three cities to ash in a moment.

shiva-tripura.ref: pathigam 6.19 (திருஆலவாய்), verse 1; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: Meru as bow and Vasuki as bowstring, he pierced the three cities of the mighty asuras with a burning arrow and turned them to ash.

shiva-tripura.ref: pathigam 6.66 (திருநாகேச்சரம்), verse 4; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: Appar at Tirunageswaram: the serpent as string, the mountain as bow, he shot and destroyed the three cities of the strong asuras.

shiva-tripura.ref: pathigam 7.99 (திருநாகேச்சரம்), verse 8; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: Sundarar at Tirunageswaram asks why the serpent had to be the string and Meru the bow just to put the three cities into the fire.

shiva-tripura.ref: Tiruvasagam section 14 (திருவுந்தியார்), verse 1; section order as listed on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: Tiruvundiyar: the bow bends, the battle breaks out, the three cities burn together.

shiva-tripura.ref: Tiruvasagam section 14 (திருவுந்தியார்), verse 2; section order as listed on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: Tiruvundiyar: we saw no second arrow in Ekambar's hand; a single arrow was enough for the three cities.

shiva-tripura.ref: Tiruvasagam section 14 (திருவுந்தியார்), verse 3; section order as listed on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: Tiruvundiyar: the chariot is let go and set aside, the axle snaps, and the three cities are destroyed (compare the broken-axle motif in Thiruppugazh song 1).

shiva-tripura.ref: pathigam 5.4 (திருஅண்ணாமலை), verse 1; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: Appar's Annamalai pathigam: almost every verse recalls that he destroyed the three cities of those who scorned him (refrain: how could I forget him).

shiva-tripura.ref: pathigam 5.4 (திருஅண்ணாமலை), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: Same pathigam: he shot the three cities of the scornful with one arrow; lord of Annamalai.

shiva-tripura.ref: pathigam 5.53 (திருஅதிகைவீரட்டம்), verse 4; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: Appar at Atigai Virattam: he set the cities of his enemies afire with his bow.

shiva-tripura.ref: pathigam 5.53 (திருஅதிகைவீரட்டம்), verse 5; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: Appar at Atigai Virattam: with the bow he shot the three cities.

shiva-tripura.ref: pathigam 3.13 (திருப்பூந்தராய்), verse 2; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: Sambandar at Poonthurai: with fiery arrows he destroyed the countless foes in the three ancient cities.

shiva-tripura.ref: pathigam 3.13 (திருப்பூந்தராய்), verse 3; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: Sambandar at Poonthurai: the proud dwellers of the three cities perished when he took up the bow.

shiva-tripura.ref: pathigam 1.82 (திருவீழிமிழலை), verse 1; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: Sambandar at Tiruveezhimizhalai: the great golden mountain as bow, fire as arrow, he destroyed the roaming three cities.

shiva-tripura.ref: pathigam 6.86 (திருவாலம்பொழில்), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-tripura.gist: Appar at Alampozhil: the serpent as string, the mountain as bow, a fire-arrow shot, he felled the great fortresses with flame.

shiva-tripura.ref: Tirumandiram, இரண்டாம் தந்திரம் - 2. பதிவலியில் வீரட்டம் எட்டு (thevaaram.org id 10202), verse 5 within the section; absolute verse number not checked
shiva-tripura.gist: Tirumandiram (eight Virattam deeds): the three cities are read as the three impurities (mala); only the wise know what burning them means.

shiva-kama.ref: pathigam 2.31 (திருக்கருப்பறியலூர்), verse 6; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-kama.gist: Sambandar at Karuppariyalur: Kama came to unite the mountain king's daughter with Shiva; the fire-spitting eye burned his body.

shiva-kama.ref: pathigam 2.3 (திருத்தெளிச்சேரி), verse 2; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-kama.gist: Sambandar at Tiruttelicheri: asks how he burned with a glance the Kama who had shot five arrows from his bow.

shiva-kama.ref: pathigam 4.14 (பொது), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-kama.gist: Appar (general pathigam): spring and cuckoo accompany Kama; sent by Vishnu he shoots; the fire of the single forehead eye reduces him to ash while the gods pray.

shiva-kama.ref: pathigam 4.25 (திருவதிகை வீரட்டானம்), verse 8; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-kama.gist: Appar at Atigai: Kama, the archer, came to the heart; Shiva burned him up with a look.

shiva-kama.ref: pathigam 4.37 (திருநெய்த்தானம்), verse 2; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-kama.gist: Appar at Neythanam: he burned Kama with a fire-glance, and gives grace to those who worship him.

shiva-kama.ref: pathigam 1.82 (திருவீழிமிழலை), verse 5; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-kama.gist: Sambandar at Tiruveezhimizhalai: Kama became ash by the fire of his eye, and he granted grace to the Lady.

shiva-kama.ref: pathigam 7.9 (திருவரிசிற்கரைப்புத்தூர்), verse 4; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-kama.gist: Sundarar at Arisilkarai-puttur: burned the three cities with one arrow, and burned the sugar-cane-bow Kama with a sidelong glance.

shiva-kama.ref: Tirumandiram, இரண்டாம் தந்திரம் - 2. பதிவலியில் வீரட்டம் எட்டு (thevaaram.org id 10202), verse 8 within the section; absolute verse number not checked
shiva-kama.gist: Tirumandiram (eight Virattam deeds): Kama's work is undone at Kurukkai; read as yogic restraint.

shiva-kama.ref: Tiruvasagam section 15 (திருத்தோணோக்கம்), verse 11; section order as listed on thevaaram.org
shiva-kama.gist: Tiruvasagam (Thonokkam): a list of those he purified/punished: Kama's body, Yama, Brahma, Daksha, Eccan, the sun and the moon.

shiva-poison.ref: pathigam 2.91 (திருமறைக்காடு), verse 7; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-poison.gist: Sambandar at Maraikkadu: serpent as rope, mountain as churning rod, gods and asuras churn; the poison rises and they flee; Shiva makes the nectar available.

shiva-poison.ref: pathigam 2.95 (திருவரசிலி), verse 6; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-poison.gist: Sambandar at Tiruvarasili: the gods churn the sea, black poison arises, and he turns it into nectar for the frightened gods.

shiva-poison.ref: pathigam 2.45 (திருக்கைச்சினம்), verse 4; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-poison.gist: Sambandar at Kaichchinam: the gods gathered and churned; the Lord swallowed the sea-poison.

shiva-poison.ref: pathigam 4.65 (திருச்சாய்க்காடு), verse 2; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-poison.gist: Appar at Chaikkadu: the gods saw the poison that rose from the churning, took refuge, and he drank it.

shiva-poison.ref: pathigam 4.70 (திருநனிபள்ளி), verse 7; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-poison.gist: Appar at Nanipalli: gods and asuras churned with the serpent and mountain; he ate the poison like nectar.

shiva-poison.ref: pathigam 6.83 (திருப்பாசூர்), verse 8; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-poison.gist: Appar at Pasur: when the gods churned the sea the Alakala poison rose and scorched the world; he swallowed it in a blink, throat darkened.

shiva-poison.ref: pathigam 6.4 (திரு அதிகை வீரட்டானம்), verse 8; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-poison.gist: Appar at Atigai: he churned the sea with the serpent around a mountain and swallowed the poison.

shiva-poison.ref: pathigam 7.55 (திருப்புன்கூர்), verse 5; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-poison.gist: Sundarar at Punkur: Meru as rod and serpent as rope, the poison rose; to save the gods he drank it and held it in his throat.

shiva-poison.ref: Tiruvasagam section 12 (திருச்சாழல்), verse 8; section order as listed on thevaaram.org
shiva-poison.gist: Tiruchchazhal: the poison that rose from the roaring sea; had he not eaten it, Brahma, Vishnu and all the gods would have died.

shiva-daksha.ref: Tirumandiram, இரண்டாம் தந்திரம் - 4. தக்கன் வேள்வி (thevaaram.org id 10204), verse 1 within the section; absolute verse number not checked
shiva-daksha.gist: Tirumandiram, whole section 'Daksha's sacrifice' (9 verses): Shiva's wrath rises from the fire, and the gods scatter; opening verse.

shiva-daksha.ref: Tirumandiram, இரண்டாம் தந்திரம் - 4. தக்கன் வேள்வி (thevaaram.org id 10204), verse 6 within the section; absolute verse number not checked
shiva-daksha.gist: Tirumandiram: Vishnu, Brahma, Daksha, the sun, the fire, the moon and Indra lose head, face, hand and shoulder without Hara's grace.

shiva-daksha.ref: Tiruvasagam section 14 (திருவுந்தியார்), verse 8; section order as listed on thevaaram.org
shiva-daksha.gist: Tiruvundiyar: Daksha, who spoke ill of Parvati's lord, is not worth looking at.

shiva-daksha.ref: Tiruvasagam section 14 (திருவுந்தியார்), verse 16; section order as listed on thevaaram.org
shiva-daksha.gist: Tiruvundiyar: Daksha lost his head that day and his sons stood around; the sacrifice was ruined.

shiva-daksha.ref: Tiruvasagam section 12 (திருச்சாழல்), verse 5; section order as listed on thevaaram.org
shiva-daksha.gist: Tiruchchazhal: why did he cut off the heads of Daksha and Eccan and kill the gathered gods? Because he then gave them grace.

shiva-daksha.ref: Tiruvasagam section 8 (திருவம்மானை), verse 15; section order as listed on thevaaram.org
shiva-daksha.gist: Tiruvammanai: moon ground down, Indra's shoulders crushed, Eccan's head cut, the sun's teeth broken, at Daksha's sacrifice.

shiva-daksha.ref: pathigam 4.65 (திருச்சாய்க்காடு), verse 5; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-daksha.gist: Appar at Chaikkadu: while the gods chanted, he destroyed the sacrifice of the cunning Daksha and favoured the moon.

shiva-daksha.ref: pathigam 6.34 (திருவாரூர்), verse 4; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-daksha.gist: Appar at Tiruvarur: recalls the day he destroyed the great sacrifice of Daksha.

shiva-daksha.ref: pathigam 6.43 (திருப்பூந்துருத்தி), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-daksha.gist: Appar at Poonthuruthi: he turned back Daksha's sacrifice, which the gods had not understood.

shiva-daksha.ref: pathigam 6.85 (திருமுண்டீச்சரம்), verse 7; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-daksha.gist: Appar at Mundicchuram: kicked Daksha's sacrifice apart and cut off Daksha's head.

shiva-daksha.ref: pathigam 1.113 (திருவல்லம்), verse 6; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-daksha.gist: Sambandar at Tiruvallam: kicked Yama for the sage, and shattered Daksha's sacrifice.

shiva-yama.ref: pathigam 4.107 (திருக்கடவூர் வீரட்டம்), verse 1; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-yama.gist: Appar at Kadavur Virattam: for the boy Markandeya he kicked fierce Yama, whose tongue lolled and fangs showed.

shiva-yama.ref: pathigam 4.107 (திருக்கடவூர் வீரட்டம்), verse 2; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-yama.gist: Appar at Kadavur: the boy worshipped chanting the five letters; Shiva kicked angry Yama so that blood ran from his eyes.

shiva-yama.ref: pathigam 4.31 (திருக்கடவூர் வீரட்டம்), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-yama.gist: Appar at Kadavur Virattam: for Markandeya, who worshipped with milk, curd and ghee, he kicked Yama.

shiva-yama.ref: pathigam 4.65 (திருச்சாய்க்காடு), verse 1; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-yama.gist: Appar at Chaikkadu: Markandeya worshipped with flowers; when Yama came for his appointed day, Shiva struck Yama down.

shiva-yama.ref: pathigam 5.66 (திருவலஞ்சுழி), verse 4; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-yama.gist: Appar at Valanchuli: he kicked cruel Yama for the boy who brought water and flowers.

shiva-yama.ref: pathigam 7.69 (வடதிருமுல்லைவாயில்), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-yama.gist: Sundarar at Mullaivayil: when Yama came against the boy worshipping with flowers, Shiva ended Yama with his foot.

shiva-yama.ref: pathigam 2.61 (திருவெண்காடு), verse 7; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-yama.gist: Sambandar at Venkadu: he destroyed Yama by his will for the boy's sake.

shiva-yama.ref: pathigam 2.101 (திருவாரூர்), verse 3; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-yama.gist: Sambandar at Tiruvarur: the Lord who drank poison also took away Yama's claim on the boy's life.

shiva-yama.ref: Tirumandiram, இரண்டாம் தந்திரம் - 2. பதிவலியில் வீரட்டம் எட்டு (thevaaram.org id 10202), verse 7 within the section; absolute verse number not checked
shiva-yama.gist: Tirumandiram (eight Virattam deeds): at Kadavur he subdues Yama; read as yogic control of breath.

shiva-yama.ref: Tiruvasagam section 9 (திருப்பொற்சுண்ணம்), verse 18; section order as listed on thevaaram.org
shiva-yama.gist: Tiruporchunnam: kicking Yama is one of the sung deeds along with Brahma's head, the elephant hide and the burning of the cities.

shiva-brahma-head.ref: pathigam 2.19 (திருநெல்லிக்கா), verse 3; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-brahma-head.gist: Sambandar at Tirunellikka: the skull-bearer holds Brahma's head.

shiva-brahma-head.ref: pathigam 3.89 (திருக்கொச்சைவயம்), verse 5; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-brahma-head.gist: Sambandar at Kochchaivayam: the Lord who cut off Brahma's head.

shiva-brahma-head.ref: pathigam 6.66 (திருநாகேச்சரம்), verse 8; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-brahma-head.gist: Appar at Tirunageswaram: cut one head of the unrighteous Brahma with a hand.

shiva-brahma-head.ref: pathigam 6.50 (திருவீழிமிழலை), verse 10; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-brahma-head.gist: Appar at Tiruveezhimizhalai: cut one of Brahma's five heads.

shiva-brahma-head.ref: pathigam 7.4 (திருவஞ்சைக்களம்), verse 8; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-brahma-head.gist: Sundarar at Anchaikkalam: crushed Ravana, drank the sea-poison, and cut one of Brahma's five heads.

shiva-brahma-head.ref: pathigam 6.34 (திருவாரூர்), verse 6; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-brahma-head.gist: Appar at Tiruvarur: begged his food with Brahma's skull in hand.

shiva-brahma-head.ref: pathigam 5.98 (பொது), verse 10; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-brahma-head.gist: Appar (general): the one who cut off Brahma's head and pressed down the demon on Kailasa.

shiva-brahma-head.ref: pathigam 4.93 (திருக்கண்டியூர் வீரட்டம்), verse 3; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-brahma-head.gist: Appar at Kandiyur Virattam: the place of the creator's severed head (verse speaks of the head of the creator).

shiva-brahma-head.ref: Tiruvasagam section 14 (திருவுந்தியார்), verse 18; section order as listed on thevaaram.org
shiva-brahma-head.gist: Tiruvundiyar: Brahma's head, on the lotus, was cut off with the nail.

shiva-brahma-head.ref: Tirumandiram, இரண்டாம் தந்திரம் - 2. பதிவலியில் வீரட்டம் எட்டு (thevaaram.org id 10202), verse 2 within the section; absolute verse number not checked
shiva-brahma-head.gist: Tirumandiram (eight Virattam deeds): the head of Brahma (Prajapati) is cut off.

shiva-bhikshatana.ref: pathigam 3.104 (திருப்பரிதிநியமம்), verse 1; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-bhikshatana.gist: Sambandar at Tiruparithiniyamam: a ten-verse refrain of the beggar who goes for alms and steals the beauty of the women's glances.

shiva-bhikshatana.ref: pathigam 3.104 (திருப்பரிதிநியமம்), verse 7; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-bhikshatana.gist: Same pathigam: going from house to house for alms, he makes women's bangles slip and steals their beauty.

shiva-bhikshatana.ref: pathigam 1.1 (திருப்பிரமபுரம்), verse 2; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-bhikshatana.gist: Sambandar's first pathigam (Tirupiramapuram): he goes for alms with a skull and the thief steals my heart.

shiva-bhikshatana.ref: pathigam 1.1 (திருப்பிரமபுரம்), verse 4; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-bhikshatana.gist: Same pathigam: eating from a skull in alms rounds, he is the thief of my heart.

shiva-bhikshatana.ref: pathigam 3.70 (திருமயிலாடுதுறை), verse 5; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-bhikshatana.gist: Sambandar at Mayiladuthurai: walks from house to house for alms among the women.

shiva-annamalai.ref: Tirumandiram, இரண்டாம் தந்திரம் - 8. அடிமுடி தேடல் (thevaaram.org id 10208), verse 1 within the section; absolute verse number not checked
shiva-annamalai.gist: Tirumandiram section 'Adimudi thedal': Brahma and Vishnu each claim to be supreme; Shiva stands as a blazing fire and they set out to seek his feet and crown.

shiva-annamalai.ref: Tirumandiram, இரண்டாம் தந்திரம் - 8. அடிமுடி தேடல் (thevaaram.org id 10208), verse 2 within the section; absolute verse number not checked
shiva-annamalai.gist: Tirumandiram: Brahma and Vishnu, the two seeking his feet and crown, fail; Achyuta says he has not found the feet.

shiva-annamalai.ref: pathigam 2.25 (திருப்புகலி), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-annamalai.gist: Sambandar at Pukali: Vishnu and Brahma seek his feet and crown while he stands as a vast flame.

shiva-annamalai.ref: pathigam 2.108 (திருவிற்குடி வீரட்டம்), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-annamalai.gist: Sambandar at Virkudi Virattam: Vishnu and Brahma sought but could not know his feet; he is fire everywhere.

shiva-annamalai.ref: pathigam 3.15 (திருவெண்காடு), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-annamalai.gist: Sambandar at Venkadu: Brahma and Vishnu searched but could not discern him.

shiva-annamalai.ref: pathigam 7.22 (திருப்பழமண்ணிப்படிக்கரை), verse 8; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-annamalai.gist: Sundarar at Pazhamannipadikkarai: Brahma and Vishnu could not see his feet or crown.

shiva-annamalai.ref: pathigam 6.40 (திருமழபாடி), verse 7; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-annamalai.gist: Appar at Mazhapadi: Vishnu and Brahma could not see him.

shiva-annamalai.ref: pathigam 5.34 (திருநெய்த்தானம்), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-annamalai.gist: Appar at Neythanam: Vishnu and Brahma could not find his feet or crown.

shiva-annamalai.ref: pathigam 4.50 (திருக்குறுக்கைவீரட்டம்), verse 1; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-annamalai.gist: Appar at Kurukkai: Vishnu and Brahma failed to find his feet or crown.

shiva-annamalai.ref: pathigam 2.117 (திருவிரும்பைமாகாளம்), verse 10; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-annamalai.gist: Sambandar at Irumbai: Brahma and Vishnu did not know his feet or crown.

shiva-annamalai.ref: pathigam 1.77 (திருஅச்சிறுபாக்கம்), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-annamalai.gist: Sambandar at Achirupakkam: Vishnu and Brahma could not see his feet or crown despite their power.

shiva-ganga.ref: pathigam 3.122 (திருஓமாம்புலியூர்), verse 3; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ganga.gist: Sambandar at Omampuliyur: he favoured the penance of Bhagiratha, hid the Ganga in his matted hair, and brought it down to earth gently.

shiva-ganga.ref: pathigam 1.104 (திருப்புகலி), verse 7; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ganga.gist: Sambandar at Pukali: hid the Ganga in his long hair along with the moon.

shiva-ganga.ref: pathigam 1.39 (திருவேட்களம்), verse 8; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ganga.gist: Sambandar at Vetkalam: the falling Ganga hidden in a lock of his matted hair.

shiva-ganga.ref: pathigam 1.105 (திருவாரூர்), verse 6; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ganga.gist: Sambandar at Tiruvarur: hid the Ganga in a long lock.

shiva-ganga.ref: pathigam 2.67 (திருப்பெரும்புலியூர்), verse 1; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ganga.gist: Sambandar at Perumpuliyur: hid the Ganga in his hair.

shiva-ganga.ref: pathigam 1.118 (திருப்பருப்பதம்), verse 8; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ganga.gist: Sambandar at Paruppatham: hid the surging Ganga in his fragrant matted hair.

shiva-ravana.ref: pathigam 3.28 (திருமழபாடி), verse 8; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ravana.gist: Sambandar at Mazhapadi: Ravana lifted Kailasa; Shiva pressed him down; Ravana cried Shiva's feet were his refuge and sang with his veins as strings.

shiva-ravana.ref: pathigam 4.49 (திருக்குறுக்கைவீரட்டம்), verse 10; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ravana.gist: Appar at Kurukkai: Ravana lifted bright Kailasa; one finger pressed him, he cried out and sang with a nerve, and was released.

shiva-ravana.ref: pathigam 6.20 (திருநள்ளாறு), verse 10; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ravana.gist: Appar at Nallaru: Ravana, sure of his boon, was crushed by the toe, then Shiva was moved by his music.

shiva-ravana.ref: pathigam 4.1 (திருவதிகை வீரட்டானம்), verse 10; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ravana.gist: Appar at Atigai: Ravana was pressed beneath the great mountain, then given grace.

shiva-ravana.ref: pathigam 5.72 (திருநீலக்குடி), verse 10; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ravana.gist: Appar at Nilakkudi: Ravana, proud, lifted the mountain; with one toe Shiva crushed him, then showed mercy.

shiva-ravana.ref: pathigam 2.20 (திருஅழுந்தூர்), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ravana.gist: Sambandar at Azhundur: Ravana lifted the mountain; Shiva crushed his body with a finger.

shiva-ravana.ref: pathigam 3.5 (திருப்பூந்தராய்), verse 8; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ravana.gist: Sambandar at Poonthurai: with one toe he destroyed Ravana's strength, then gave grace.

shiva-ravana.ref: pathigam 2.59 (சீகாழி), verse 8; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ravana.gist: Sambandar at Kali: Ravana's crowns and shoulders were crushed by the Lord, who gives grace to devotees.

shiva-dakshinamurti.ref: pathigam 4.36 (திருப்பழனம்), verse 6; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-dakshinamurti.gist: Appar at Pazhanam: under the banyan he taught the dharmas to the four, the subtle meaning of every text.

shiva-dakshinamurti.ref: pathigam 6.66 (திருநாகேச்சரம்), verse 2; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-dakshinamurti.gist: Appar at Tirunageswaram: seated under the banyan he taught the four (dharma, wealth, pleasure, liberation) with the six Angas and the Vedas.

shiva-dakshinamurti.ref: pathigam 6.74 (திருநாரையூர்), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-dakshinamurti.gist: Appar at Naraiyur: under the banyan he taught the four.

shiva-dakshinamurti.ref: pathigam 6.30 (திருவாரூர்), verse 3; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-dakshinamurti.gist: Appar at Tiruvarur: under the stone banyan he taught dharma.

shiva-dakshinamurti.ref: pathigam 6.22 (திருநாகைக் காரோணம்), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-dakshinamurti.gist: Appar at Nagai-Karonam: taught the Vedas to the four sages under the banyan.

shiva-dakshinamurti.ref: pathigam 6.23 (திருமறைக்காடு), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-dakshinamurti.gist: Appar at Maraikkadu: the teacher of dharma to the four under the banyan.

shiva-dakshinamurti.ref: pathigam 2.24 (திருநாகேச்சரம்), verse 3; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-dakshinamurti.gist: Sambandar at Nageswaram: he who abides in the shade of the stone banyan.

shiva-dakshinamurti.ref: pathigam 5.8 (திருஅன்னியூர்), verse 8; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-dakshinamurti.gist: Appar at Anniyur: seated beneath the banyan teaching dharma.

shiva-dakshinamurti.ref: pathigam 7.99 (திருநாகேச்சரம்), verse 2; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-dakshinamurti.gist: Sundarar at Tirunageswaram: asks why he sat under the banyan teaching dharma to the great ascetics.

shiva-dakshinamurti.ref: pathigam 1.41 (திருப்பாம்புரம்), verse 7; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-dakshinamurti.gist: Sambandar at Tirupamburam: gave grace to the four under the banyan; also kicked Yama and burned Kama.

shiva-dakshinamurti.ref: Tiruvasagam section 12 (திருச்சாழல்), verse 16; section order as listed on thevaaram.org
shiva-dakshinamurti.gist: Tiruchchazhal: under the banyan he taught the four the secret of the four Vedas.

shiva-ardhanari.ref: pathigam 4.7 (திருக்கச்சியேகம்பம்), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ardhanari.gist: Appar at Ekambam: the Lord whose body is half male, half female.

shiva-ardhanari.ref: pathigam 4.36 (திருப்பழனம்), verse 7; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ardhanari.gist: Appar at Pazhanam: the Lord who took the form of half woman.

shiva-ardhanari.ref: pathigam 5.29 (திருவாவடுதுறை), verse 3; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ardhanari.gist: Appar at Avaduthurai: the Lord with a woman as half; the Light.

shiva-ardhanari.ref: pathigam 5.97 (பொது), verse 3; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ardhanari.gist: Appar (general): half-woman form, the Light within the Light.

shiva-ardhanari.ref: pathigam 6.38 (திருவையாறு), verse 5; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ardhanari.gist: Appar at Aiyaru: you are male and female, birthless.

shiva-ardhanari.ref: pathigam 6.18 (திருப்பூவணம்), verse 2; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ardhanari.gist: Appar at Tiruppuvanam: appears in a form both male and female.

shiva-ardhanari.ref: pathigam 4.18 (பொது), verse 2; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-ardhanari.gist: Appar (general): the two ear-ornaments, one male, one female; the Lord of the dual form.

shiva-nataraja.ref: pathigam 4.81 (கோயில்), verse 4; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-nataraja.gist: Appar's Tillai verse: the curved brow, red lips, gentle smile, matted hair and the raised golden foot: the vision of the dancing Lord.

shiva-nataraja.ref: pathigam 4.22 (கோயில்), verse 2; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-nataraja.gist: Appar at Tillai: the Lord with the Ganga in his hair and the Lady at his side dances in the blazing fire in the Chitrambalam.

shiva-nataraja.ref: pathigam 3.1 (கோயில்), verse 1; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-nataraja.gist: Sambandar at Tillai: praises the Lord bathed in ghee, milk and curd who abides in the Chitrambalam of the Tillai Brahmins.

shiva-nataraja.ref: Tiruvasagam section 12 (திருச்சாழல்), verse 14; section order as listed on thevaaram.org
shiva-nataraja.gist: Tiruchchazhal: why does the Lord of Tillai's Chitrambalam dance? Because if he did not, the world would be filled with Kali's flesh-eating company.

shiva-nataraja.ref: pathigam 6.34 (திருவாரூர்), verse 8; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-nataraja.gist: Appar at Tiruvarur: he protected Muyalakan with his foot.

shiva-nataraja.ref: pathigam 6.90 (திருக்கஞ்சனூர்), verse 9; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-nataraja.gist: Appar at Kanchanur: he set his foot on Muyalakan.

shiva-nataraja.ref: pathigam 6.96 (பொது), verse 3; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-nataraja.gist: Appar (general): with ringing anklets, he keeps the unruly Muyalakan beneath his foot.

shiva-nataraja.ref: pathigam 4.100 (திருவின்னம்பர்), verse 7; Tirumurai.pathigam.verse as numbered on thevaaram.org
shiva-nataraja.gist: Appar at Innambar: feet that quell the rage of the vile Muyalakan.

shiva-nataraja.ref: Tirumandiram, ஒன்பதாம் தந்திரம் - 15. அற்புதக் கூத்து (thevaaram.org id 10915), verse 13 within the section; absolute verse number not checked
shiva-nataraja.gist: Tirumandiram 'Adbhuta Koothu': Muyalakan appears as the ego (ahankara); the Lord dances in the great hall of space.
